parts.article:
A study of western celebrity
 
In our celebrity-obsessed culture, TV shows, internet blogs, and even newspapers are often full of the latest news, gossip and scandals about current celebrities
 
(A) It seems that our current society cannot get enough information about the daily lives of celebrities. But how did celebrities become such an important force in our culture? While people have always shared a certain obsession with the fantastic and the famous, the notion of celebrity, as well as the types of people termed 'celebrities', has evolved greatly throughout the ages. The word 'celebrity' has its roots in the language of the ancient Roman civilization. The word we now know to mean 'a condition of being famous' or 'a famous person' is derived from the Latin word 'celeber', meaning 'frequented or populous'.
 
(B) The celebrities of the ancient world were the powerful and awesome deities of Greece and Rome, and the citizens of these civilizations believed in a vast number of immortals who had a direct impact on their lives. It was, therefore, important to know about these figures' personal lives. This need to know led to the creation of myths, which personalized the gods and involved them in ancient celebrity scandals that thrilled and excited the common people.
 
(C) During ancient times, amateur and professional athletes also began to make an impact on the celebrity culture. Victors in the ancient Olympic Games were treated as heroes and were often elevated to god-like status. In the ancient Roman civilization, gladiators – the equivalent of today's professional athletes – were also revered by the common people for their heroics and seemingly superhuman strength.
 
(D) As Europe moved into the Dark Ages (the years spanning approximately 400–1300 AD) and a time when athletics and the arts were largely forgotten, monarchs and rulers continued to maintain celebrity status, while religious figures took on newfound fame. The miraculous lives and fascinating deaths of spiritual figures lent excitement to the lives of common people when there was often little else to be excited about, as they faced war, disease and food shortages.
 
(E) During the period 1300–1600 AD, or the Renaissance period as it is known, interest in ruling figures faded. As Europe emerged from its long neglect of the arts, there was greater appreciation for portraits, statues and stone carvings. This period of appreciation for the arts lent a sense of celebrity to artists who were noted for their works and their personal achievements. It was a time when artists began to surpass political and religious individuals for supreme celebrity – a trend that would continue into later centuries.
 
(F) While the figures of the ancient and early modern civilizations were able to achieve moderate and sometimes lasting celebrity within particular cultures, the global reach of their fame was limited. It was not until the 1700s, when technological advances made publishing commercially viable, that the extent of a person's fame could spread further. The increase in the availability of the written word was accompanied by a huge rise in the number of common people who could read, allowing a mass audience to find out about celebrities for the first time. Suddenly, the lives of authors, politicians, war heroes, and other celebrities could now be read about in newspapers around the world. These gave ordinary people the opportunity to become intimately knowledgeable about the figures they most admired.
 
(G) In the modern era, particularly as radio and film took off in the 1900s, things really began to change. First, radio began to make its way into the average home in the 1920s and 1930s. Professional athletes also began to be regarded as stars, as their games and exploits could be broadcast over the air for an entirely new audience. Then, the rise of television in the 1950s only cemented the premier level of celebrity that film stars, athletes and television actors were beginning to share. This also meant a huge increase in the individual salaries of these celebrities. Even a few animals gained fame through children's TV shows. The emergence of reality television shows in the late 1990s allowed all kinds of people with little ability to enjoy a short burst of fame on the television screen. All you needed, it seemed, was an attractive appearance. Today, reality television programmers make it possible to be famous not for doing anything in particular, but simply for being, with the audience deciding whether someone deserves to become a celebrity or not. As the meaning of celebrity continues to evolve and redefine itself in a quickly changing world, there is no telling who will become of interest next.

analyses.content: 只有这一段在从语言学角度解释这个单词的来源（roots/derived from），所以一定是“original definition”。
(Paragraph A) “The word 'celebrity' has its roots in the language of the ancient Roman civilization... derived from the Latin word 'celeber'...”
A段结尾直接解释了“celebrity”这个词源于拉丁语“celeber”及其本义，这正是对该词的最初定义，对应选项 x。
B段的主角是神和神话人物（deities/immortals），即“非人类”，并描述了它们对人们生活的直接影响，对应选项 ii。
这里的“non-human celebrities”指的就是段落中的“deities”和“gods”，不要因为没看到“non-human”这个词就略过。
(Paragraph B) “The celebrities of the ancient world were the powerful and awesome deities... believed in a vast number of immortals who had a direct impact on their lives.”
C段讲述了古代奥运冠军和角斗士因其英雄气概和超人的力量（strength）而受到崇拜，这些都属于身体成就，对应选项 v。
“Physical achievement” 是对 “athletes”、“victors”、“gladiators” 以及 “superhuman strength” 的概括。
(Paragraph C) “...gladiators... were also revered by the common people for their heroics and seemingly superhuman strength.”
“Hardship” 是对文中 “war, disease and food shortages” 的完美总结。
D段提到在黑暗时代，人们面临战争、疾病和食物短缺（food shortages）等困境，宗教人物的事迹成了他们在这些艰难中的精神慰藉，对应选项 vii（苦难的结果）。
(Paragraph D) “...lent excitement to the lives of common people... as they faced war, disease and food shortages.”
E段（文艺复兴时期）提到人们开始欣赏艺术，艺术家（artists）的地位开始超越统治者，说明创造力（creativity）获得了更大的价值，对应选项 iv。
“Creativity” 对应段落中的 “artists” 和 “works”，而 “greater value” 对应 “surpass political and religious individuals”。
(Paragraph E) “It was a time when artists began to surpass political and religious individuals for supreme celebrity...”
F段提到1700年代出版业发展，识字（read）人数大增，这使得名人的名声能首次传播给大众（mass audience），对应选项 viii（识字与广泛的名人效应）。
必须同时看到“literacy”（对应文中 rise in people who could read）和“widespread”（对应 spread further / mass audience）。
(Paragraph F) “The increase in the availability of the written word was accompanied by a huge rise in the number of common people who could read...”
(Paragraph G) “In the modern era, particularly as radio and film took off... Then, the rise of television...”
“Broadcasting” 涵盖了段落中提到的 radio, film, television。
G段讨论了无线电、电影、电视特别是真人秀（broadcasting）的兴起如何改变了名人的定义（只需外表，甚至动物也能成名），对应选项 iii。

questions.question: A wide variety of people achieve a brief period of fame.

analyses.content: G段（Modern era）提到真人秀让“all kinds of people（各种各样的人）”享受“short burst of fame（短暂的成名）”，对应选项 D。
“Brief period” 对应 “short burst”，且这是现代（Modern era）真人秀的特征。
(Paragraph G) “The emergence of reality television shows... allowed all kinds of people... to enjoy a short burst of fame...”

questions.question: Stories are invented about celebrities' lives.

analyses.content: B段（Ancient times）提到为了了解神的生活，导致了“creation of myths（神话的创造）”，神话即编造的故事，对应选项 A。
“Invented” 对应 “creation”，且神话（myths）本质上就是虚构的故事。
(Paragraph B) “This need to know led to the creation of myths, which personalized the gods...”

questions.question: The fame of rulers is starting to diminish.

analyses.content: (Paragraph E) “During the period 1300–1600 AD... interest in ruling figures faded.”
E段（Renaissance）开头明确说“interest in ruling figures faded（对统治人物的兴趣消退了）”，对应选项 C。
“Diminish” 是 “faded” 的同义替换，定位非常直接。

groups.contentHtml: The development of the publishing industry in the 1700s signalled the beginning of international fame. A growing number of people could read, which meant they had the chance to become informed about their favourite figures by reading . This exposure to celebrities expanded further when radio and television became popular, and it was mass media attention that resulted in higher status and fame for some celebrities. The recent rise of reality television has also meant that a person's rather than their talent can bring fame. With this type of television programme, fame may be entirely dependent on the response of the .

analyses.content: 题目说人们可以通过阅读____来了解他们喜爱的人物，原文F段提到人们第一次可以在世界各地的“newspapers”上读到名人的生活，填 newspapers。
题目中的 “informed about” 对应原文的 “find out about” 或 “read about”。
(Paragraph F) “Suddenly, the lives of authors... could now be read about in newspapers around the world.”
题目说现在一个人的____而不是才华能带来名气，原文G段提到在真人秀时代，似乎只需要迷人的“appearance（外表）”，填 appearance。
题目中的 “rather than their talent” 对应原文的 “people with little ability”。
(Paragraph G) “All you needed, it seemed, was an attractive appearance.”
题目说名气可能完全取决于____的反应，原文G段最后说由“audience（观众）”来决定某人是否值得成为名人，填 audience。
“Dependent on the response of” 对应原文的 “with the audience deciding”。
(Paragraph G) “...with the audience deciding whether someone deserves to become a celebrity or not.”
